title: Ordinary and locally adaptive IBM smoothing
text: package uses augmented state x(t)=(f′(t),f(t))𝖳x(t)=(f'(t),f(t))^\mathsf T. [tj,tj+1][t_j,t_{j+1}], Δj=tj+1−tj\Delta_j=t_{j+1}-t_j, xj+1∣xj,λj∼N2{Ajxj,λjQj},Aj=(10Δj1),Qj=(ΔjΔj2/2Δj2/2Δj3/3). x_{j+1}\mid x_j,\lambda_j\sim N_2\{A_jx_j,\lambda_jQ_j\}, \quad A_j=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\Delta_j&1\end{pmatrix}, \quad Q_j=\begin{pmatrix} \Delta_j&\Delta_j^2/2\\ \Delta_j^2/2&\Delta_j^3/3 \end{pmatrix}. exact transition irregular grids. finite-difference approximation replace observed time operational time.

title: Ordinary and locally adaptive IBM smoothing
text: Ordinary IBM uses one diffusion standard deviation τ\tau, λj=τ2\lambda_j=\tau^2. smoothing_prior accepts valid Stan code involving positive parameter tau. tau constrained positive, symmetric Stan distributions examples induce corresponding truncated (half) distributions. Priors specified internally standardized response time scale.
code: fit_lognormal <- ibm(t, y)  fit_half_normal <- ibm(   t, y,   smoothing_prior = "tau ~ normal(0, 0.5);" )  fit_half_t <- ibm(   t, y,   smoothing_prior = "tau ~ student_t(3, 0, 0.5);" )

title: Ordinary and locally adaptive IBM smoothing
text: adaptive model uses λj=γξj,ξj∼C+(0,1),γ∼C+(0,sγ). \sqrt{\lambda_j}=\gamma\xi_j,\qquad \xi_j\sim C^+(0,1),\qquad \gamma\sim C^+(0,s_\gamma). intervals can strongly regularized heavy-tailed local scales allow selected intervals substantially larger derivative innovations. derivative remains continuous Brownian path; local scale controls much slope permitted evolve interval. Posterior samples function derivative available directly:
code: fit_adaptive <- ibm(   t, y,   adaptive = TRUE,   global_scale = 0.1,   chains = 4,   iter = 2000,   adapt_delta = 0.99 )  plot(fit_adaptive) plot_diffusion(fit_adaptive) summary(fit_adaptive) f_draws <- get_samples(fit_adaptive, "f") derivative_draws <- get_samples(fit_adaptive, "fprime") lambda_draws <- get_samples(fit_adaptive, "lambda_interval")

title: Integrated Brownian Motion Smoothing
text: ibmsmooth fits integrated Brownian motion smoothers Gaussian observations using Stan. package intentionally contains two models: ordinary IBM one positive smoothing parameter user-supplied Stan prior parameter; locally adaptive IBM horseshoe global–local shrinkage derivative diffusion rate. locations (t_j<t_{j+1}), (j=t{j+1}-t_j), state (x_j=(f’(t_j),f(t_j))^T), models use exact transition [ x_{j+1}x_j,_j  N_2. ] Ordinary IBM sets (_j=^2). adaptive model sets (_j=2_j2), (_j^+(0,1)) (^+(0,)).

title: Integrated Brownian Motion Smoothing
text: data standardized internally, custom smoothing priors specified standardized model scale. Extraction functions transform posterior draws back original response time scales.
code: library(ibmsmooth)  fit <- ibm(t, y)  # Any valid Stan prior statement involving the positive parameter `tau`. fit_half_t <- ibm(   t, y,   smoothing_prior = "tau ~ student_t(3, 0, 0.5);" )  fit_adaptive <- ibm(   t, y,   adaptive = TRUE,   global_scale = 0.1 )  plot(fit_adaptive) plot_diffusion(fit_adaptive)
